solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Getting sadder, possibly notices people getting the message?

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of sadder are only one arrangement and may be shuffled into another

parts.note: to notice something is to see it, so notices gives sees

explanation.surface: Someone grows sadder as they read notices of bad news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges SADDER into ADDRES. The question mark warns that the definition is cryptic: people getting a message receive it rather than understand it.
explanation.definitionFit: Those to whom a letter or message is sent are its recipients, the people it is directed at.

clue.text: Is a cafe almost falling apart? Look at this above its window

definitions.text: Look at this above its window

indicators.note: a building falling apart is breaking up, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt
almost the whole word cafe means it loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A shabby cafe is crumbling; look up at the sign above its window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims CAFE to CAF; 'falling apart' then rearranges ISACAF.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop's name board, fixed over the front window, is called by this term; the clue invites the eye up to that sign.

clue.text: Poison can make you a bit upset before long

indicators.note: before places the earlier piece ahead of the one for long
in a down clue upset turns the word upside down, so it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an ort is a scrap or small bit left over from a meal
to long for something is to pine for it

explanation.surface: Someone warns that a poison will soon leave you a little ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ORT into TRO. ORT, a scrap, is a crossword favourite. The blog notes that this drug is a poison only in overdose.
explanation.definitionFit: The alkaloid from deadly nightshade is toxic in quantity, hence a poison, though it has medical uses.

clue.text: Hairstyle of supermodel

indicators.note: of says the letters come out of the word supermodel, sitting inside it

explanation.surface: We are told about a famous model's hairdo.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemically set wave or curl is a classic salon hairdo, short for permanent wave.

clue.text: Writer having restricted outlook from Iberia?

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument, a writer in crossword terms
an insular person is narrow-minded, with a limited view of the world

explanation.surface: A narrow-minded author is asked whether they come from Spain or Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: Iberia is the Peninsula of the Peninsular War; the question mark flags the indirect definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain and Portugal form the Iberian peninsula, so things from there are adjectivally described this way, as in the Peninsular War.

clue.text: What you expect to find written round bad monument?

indicators.note: written round says the first piece is set down encircling the second

parts.note: par is the norm, what one expects
ill can mean bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: A puzzle asks what inscription you would expect around a bad memorial.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall column put up to commemorate someone or something is a kind of monument.

clue.text: Sunhat I'd chucked, something flowery

indicators.note: chucked about means thrown around, so the letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone throws off their sun hat, which was decorated with flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinks and carnations belong to this genus, so it is a flowering plant.

clue.text: Guerrilla can also appear with this remarkable person

definitions.text: Guerrilla can also appear with this
definitions.meaning: guerrilla has an alternative spelling, guerilla, with a single R
a one-off, someone exceptional, in British slang

explanation.surface: A fighter's name is spelt variously, and someone is rather special.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is cryptic: the variant spelling guerilla has a single R, so the letters are read as ONE R.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses this word for a unique or outstanding individual, a one-of-a-kind character.

clue.text: Do I need it, read it, ultimately averse to change?

definitions.text: Do I need it, read it, ultimately averse to change?

indicators.note: to change says the letters gathered are to be altered into a fresh order

parts.words: Do I need it, read it
parts.note: these words are the anagram fodder; as printed they carry a second I too many, a slip Bradman owned up to on the blog

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word averse

explanation.surface: A reader wonders whether they need the printed paper, being stubbornly resistant to change.
explanation.walkthrough: Setter's slip: the anagram needs DO NEED IT READ IT plus E; the printed 'I' is one too many, as Bradman admitted. The whole clue is the reader of print who resists going digital.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper copy of a newspaper, printed on wood pulp, is jokingly so called by those who read online.

clue.text: Page in directory

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the word directory

explanation.surface: We are directed to a page in a directory.
explanation.definitionFit: The right-hand page of an open book, the front of a leaf, is a printing term for a page.

clue.text: User of ship going by sea

indicators.note: going by means passing alongside, so one piece sits next to the other

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the open sea
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: Someone uses a ship to travel by sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'User' looks like a passenger, but it means a drug addict.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who injects drugs straight into a vein is a drug user, so this addict is a user.

clue.text: Europeans in south with awful rain penetrating homes?

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south

indicators.note: penetrating means getting inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: pads are slang for homes or flats

indicators.note: awful suggests the word rain is in a terrible mess and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: People living in the south find dreadful rain getting into their houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges RAIN into ANIAR. 'homes' is slang PADS, not houses as such.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives of Spain are European people, so they are Europeans.

clue.text: One may be losing too many trees as frontier is shifted

definitions.text: One may be losing too many trees

indicators.note: something shifted is moved about, so these letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: A forest is cut back too much as the border moves.
explanation.definitionFit: Tropical jungles such as the Amazon suffer from deforestation, so this is a habitat losing trees.

clue.text: Graduate female's suffering setback — restorative treatment needed

indicators.note: suffering a setback here means being sent backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
her is the female possessive pronoun

explanation.surface: A woman graduate has had a setback and needs recovery treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for rehabilitation, it is a programme helping someone recover, usually from addiction.

clue.text: Having two things to carry makes one unbalanced

definitions.text: Having two things to carry makes one unbalanced

parts.words: Having two things to carry makes one unbalanced
parts.note: a basket and a case are two things for carrying, and together they name a person who is mentally unbalanced

explanation.surface: Carrying two loads at once throws you off balance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unbalanced' looks physical, but it means unhinged.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, someone who cannot cope and has lost their mental balance is called this, a hopeless wreck.

clue.text: They deal with medical problems sorting out oldies with impetigos

indicators.note: sorting out puts things in order, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Doctors deal with elderly people who have a skin infection.
explanation.walkthrough: Impetigo is a contagious skin infection.
explanation.definitionFit: Scientists who study the spread and control of diseases in populations deal with medical problems.

clue.text: Violent event? As one of the detectives, gets dispatched first off

parts.note: someone who is one of the detectives is in the CID, the Criminal Investigation Department

indicators.note: first off says the opening letter is removed

parts.note: something that gets dispatched is sent

explanation.surface: A detective is sent out to a violent crime.
explanation.walkthrough: The CID is the detective branch of a British police force. 'first off' takes S from SENT, leaving ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent clash or occurrence, especially one involving police, is reported as this kind of occurrence.

clue.text: Being nasty increased a great deal, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: grew means increased; some, said with emphasis, means a great deal, as in that was some storm

explanation.surface: Someone's nastiness has grown a lot, according to reports.
explanation.definitionFit: Something horrible or repugnant is nasty in the extreme, so being nasty describes it.

clue.text: Gets rid of jazz instrument's sound

indicators.note: sound says it is the spoken form of the words before that matters

parts.note: the sax, short for saxophone, is a jazz instrument; with the possessive it is sax's

explanation.surface: Someone throws out a jazz instrument because of its noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone from a job is to dismiss them; the verb means gets rid of.

clue.text: One's in hide to see bird

indicators.note: in puts the first piece inside the word for hide

parts.note: a hide is an animal's skin
one's is I'S, with I as the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher sits in a hide to spot a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' looks like a birdwatching shelter, but it is SKIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A small yellow-green finch is a songbird, so it is a bird.

clue.text: Plan supporting Greek character with others given backing

parts.note: to be for something is to support it
mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: given backing means turned back, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: et al is Latin shorthand for and others

explanation.surface: A plan backs a Greek with help from others.
explanation.definitionFit: To devise or draw up a scheme carefully is to plan it.

clue.text: A number in camp getting shelter

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for number inside the word for camp

parts.note: a camp is a faction, as a wing of a party

explanation.surface: Someone in a campsite finds shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'camp' suggests tents, but means a faction, WING.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas sheet stretched over a window or shopfront gives cover from sun or rain, a shelter.

clue.text: New deal on street — fellow deceived

indicators.note: new indicates the word deal is made over, its letters rearranged

parts.note: Ray is a man's name, a fellow

explanation.surface: A man has been cheated in a new deal on the street.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead someone astray is to mislead them, so the past form means misled or deceived.

clue.text: Legislation has finally taken what should be green

parts.note: law is legislation

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of taken

explanation.surface: A green-energy law has at last been passed.
explanation.definitionFit: A grassed garden area is ideally kept a healthy green colour.

clue.text: Royal house delivery when Queen is out

indicators.note: is out means the queen's letters are removed from the cricket word

parts.note: a yorker is a cricket delivery pitched at the batter's feet
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the queen

explanation.surface: Something is delivered to a palace while the Queen is away.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a delivery is a ball bowled; ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The English dynasty of Edward IV and Richard III is a royal house.

clue.text: Chinese wickedness — something very cold putting English off–

parts.note: sin is wickedness

indicators.note: putting something off here means taking it away, so the abbreviation for English goes
off completes putting off, the signal that a letter is removed from the word for something very cold

parts.note: ice is very cold

explanation.surface: Chinese wickedness is chilling enough to put the English off.
explanation.definitionFit: This rare adjective, from Sina, the Latin for China, means relating to China, i.e. Chinese.

clue.text: Music-makers come first with awful noise, play badly — gents no good!

parts.note: to come first is to win
a din is an awful noise
to strum is to play idly or carelessly on strings

indicators.note: no good drops G, the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Musicians winning a contest make a terrible noise, playing badly, the men hopeless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no good' removes G (good) from GENTS, giving ENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Flutes, clarinets and trumpets are played by blowing, and they make music.
